target_audience.primary_persona: Health-conscious individuals interested in quantified self and life tracking who want to monitor habits, moods, activities, and personal metrics
secondary_personas: People managing mental health through mood tracking
Fitness enthusiasts tracking workouts and physical metrics
Privacy-focused users who want local-first data ownership
Journaling enthusiasts who prefer structured data capture
Developers and tech-savvy users comfortable with self-hosting
pain_points: Existing tracking apps don't allow custom metrics
Commercial apps collect and monetize personal health data
Unable to correlate different aspects of life (mood, sleep, exercise)
Tracking apps are too complex or too simple for personal needs
Want to track people/relationships alongside activities
Need flexible note-taking with structured data extraction
goals: Understand patterns in their daily life and habits
Improve health and well-being through data-driven insights
Track streaks and maintain habit consistency
Correlate different life factors to find what affects their mood/health
Keep private data under their own control
target_audience.usage_context: Daily use on mobile (primary) and desktop for quick tracking throughout the day, with periodic review of analytics and trends. Used during morning/evening routines or spontaneously when tracking events occur.

product_vision.one_liner: An open-source life tracker and data journal that lets you track anything using natural language with hashtags
product_vision.problem_statement: People want to track various aspects of their life (mood, habits, activities, health) but existing solutions are either too rigid, too complex, or compromise privacy by storing data in proprietary clouds. Users need a flexible, privacy-respecting way to capture and analyze personal data.
product_vision.value_proposition: Nomie offers complete tracking flexibility through its hashtag-based system (#mood(8) #walked(4)), local-first data storage with optional sync, and the ability to track anything from simple counters to complex timed activities. Unlike commercial alternatives, users own their data completely.
success_metrics: Active daily users maintaining tracking habits
Number of custom trackers created per user

known_gaps: iOS native app distribution (in progress via Capacitor)
HealthKit integration for iOS (designed, not implemented)
Widget for home screen quick logging
technical_debt: Stats module refactoring needed (Stats2 exists alongside original)
LedgerStore is complex and needs modularization
Some test coverage gaps in key modules
Export functionality needs improvements for notes
Multiple TODO comments throughout codebase (~20 documented)

differentiators: Hashtag-based natural language tracking is more flexible than fixed forms
Open-source with full data ownership and privacy
Track anything: metrics, people, contexts, locations
Correlation analysis between any tracked items
competitive_context.market_position: Positioned for privacy-conscious quantified-self enthusiasts who want complete flexibility and data ownership. Fills the gap between rigid commercial trackers and complex spreadsheet solutions. Appeals to the self-hosting and open-source community.

technical: PWA limitations on iOS (notification restrictions, background sync limits)
HealthKit only available on iOS native apps
Cross-device sync requires CouchDB server setup
Svelte 4 framework (not yet migrated to Svelte 5)
resources: Small core maintainer team (2-3 active contributors)
dependencies: Apple Developer Program for iOS App Store distribution
